record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Classify all rational cuspidal plane curves and all elliptic cuspidal plane curves.

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 1. Classify all rational and elliptic cuspidal plane curves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the complex numbers. A plane curve is an irreducible reduced algebraic curve $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$. A point $p \in C$ is called a cusp (a unibranch singular point) if the analytic local ring of $C$ at $p$ has a single branch, i.e., the germ $(C,p)$ is locally irreducible but singular. A curve $C$ is called cuspidal if every singular point of $C$ is a cusp. The geometric genus of $C$ is the genus of its normalization $\widetilde{C}$.

Provide a complete classification, up to the action of $\mathrm{PGL}(3,\mathbb{C})$ on $\mathbb{P}^2$, of:
(a) all rational cuspidal plane curves, i.e., cuspidal curves $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2$ of geometric genus $0$;
(b) all elliptic cuspidal plane curves, i.e., cuspidal curves $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2$ of geometric genus $1$.

Equivalently, list all possible degrees, configurations of cusp singularity types (topological types of unibranch local singularities), and projective equivalence classes that can be realized by such curves.
artifact.status_search_result: The full classification of rational and elliptic cuspidal plane curves up to projective equivalence remains open in general. Substantial partial progress exists: rational unicuspidal curves with one Puiseux pair have been classified (Fernández de Bobadilla–Luengo–Melle-Hernández–Némethi); the long-standing conjecture that any rational cuspidal plane curve has at most four cusps was proved by Koras and Palka via the almost minimal model program; many further structural results and constraints on singularity types are known. However, a complete classification of all rational (and a fortiori all elliptic) cuspidal plane curves is still not available.

status_evidence.title: On rational cuspidal projective plane curves
status_evidence.snippet: The classification of such curves, up to the action of PGL(3,C) on P^2, is a very difficult open problem with many interesting connections.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of rational cuspidal plane curves up to PGL(3,C) is described as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Classification of Rational Unicuspidal Projective Curves whose Singularities Have one Puiseux Pair
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of rational unicuspidal projective curves whose singularities have one Puiseux pair.
status_evidence.claim: A subclass (rational unicuspidal with one Puiseux pair) has been completely classified, indicating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Rational Cuspidal Curves (Moe thesis)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of results on rational cuspidal curves; full classification not yet achieved.
status_evidence.claim: Survey work confirms the general classification problem remains incomplete.
